answers.text: I'm a final-year BSc Physics student. Last summer I spent eight weeks as an intern at a national research institute, helping with a thin-film measurement experiment. My job was to record readings, about 120 in all, and plot them. I enjoyed the work but realised that I like asking why a lab's equipment is bought and how projects are chosen more than the experiments. That is why I want an MBA.
As secretary of the Physics Association I ran six weekly problem-solving sessions for juniors. Attendance was low at first, so I moved them to the evening after classes and it improved.
In the internship I supervised three other interns and set their daily targets. It was the first time I managed a small team.
I can't share the details of the thin-film results. The lab asked interns not to discuss unpublished data, so I can only describe the method in general terms.
I think that's enough for today. Could we end the session here? I'd like to see my feedback now.
